survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive results (means and proficiency-level shares) for Viet Nam using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The note does not describe the microdata extraction steps or whether complex survey weights (e.g., student/sampling weights and replicate weights) were applied in the computations shown. For PISA analyses, analysts typically use the provided sampling weights to account for the stratified, clustered design and to produce population-representative estimates; replicate weights are used for variance estimation when available. Because this factsheet does not specify weight variables or replicate procedures, the safest interpretation is that the published estimates already incorporate the PISA technical standards and weighting/variance methods, but the exact weight variable names are not reported here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This factsheet reports proficiency-level shares and mean performance summaries rather than providing an ML model or a documented PV-based estimation procedure in the text. This is therefore a reporting gap for PV/missing-data handling details at the factsheet level, even though the underlying OECD PISA database and technical standards would normally address these issues.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Viet Nam factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students performed in mathematics, reading, and science using PISA 2022 results from the OECD PISA 2022 Database. Viet Nam participated in PISA 2022 with 6,068 students in 178 schools, and the assessment was a two-hour paper-and-pencil test with multiple-choice and constructed-response items, complemented by student and school questionnaires. The factsheet reports mean performance relative to the OECD average and proficiency-level distributions (e.g., shares at Level 5/6 and Level 2+), and it highlights within-country performance gaps by socio-economic status (ESCS quintiles) and gender differences. It also provides contextual indicators on school belonging, discipline and support in mathematics lessons, safety and bullying, parental involvement, and learning during COVID-related closures. Methodologically, the note emphasizes that Viet Nam met PISA technical standards in 2022, but comparability for reading trends is not strong, so trend comparisons are limited.

Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally empty, and the focus is on reporting PISA achievement summaries and contextual correlates rather than an analytic modeling pipeline.
